name: Karachi Biennale Trust
funding: Philanthropists and corporate sponsors, not itemised.
watch: Name to know: K-Electric, Karachi's mostly thermal power utility. Engro (Thar coal) was KB22 lead partner. 2019 censorship row.
why_flagged: Name to know: K-Electric, Karachi's mostly thermal power utility. Engro (Thar coal) was KB22 lead partner. 2019 censorship row.
records_note: It posts a trustee list of ten names and sponsor logos by edition (KB24 partners), but no annual report and no accounts.

name: Gaza Biennale
funding: 2024-25: aimed to raise $90,000 for artists; sponsor Al Risan Art Museum, plus small partners per pavilion and private donations.
watch: Listed in the e-flux directory; no funder information found. Decentralised, crowdfunded project; pavilion partners vary by city. It staged a protest at the ICA against Bloomberg in Jan 2025 and was not a target.
records_note: Its own site sits behind a bot check, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; only press coverage was readable.

name: A.M. Qattan Foundation
funding: Income GBP 2.6M (2025): Al-Qattan Charitable Trust, Qattan family gifts, Save the Children, Drosos, Taawon, Enabel, Arts Council England, Art Fund.
watch: No adverse finding; current funder roster not checked. Barclays (under campaign) is one of its bankers, not a funder. Trust funding paused in 2025 pending a Jersey licence, not as punishment.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2005 to 2025, files audited accounts with the Charity Commission, names donors in its 2025 report, and lists its trustees.

name: Riwaq Biennale
funding: Riwaq NGO: EU, Sweden, Germany/KfW, UNDP, UNESCO, ALIPH, British Council CPF, Ford, Open Society, Prince Claus, Doen, Arab Fund, OPEC Fund.
watch: Funders not itemised. OPEC Fund for International Development (oil-state money) is on Riwaq's donor list. Last full biennale 2014; 2019 Chicago edition.
records_note: Riwaq posts annual reports for 2010 to 2025, an auditor's report in 2025, an undated named donor list, and its board in each report.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Panamá
funding: Private non-profit funded by companies and art lovers. Naturgy, a gas and electricity group, signed a sponsorship in April 2023 covering upkeep and operations.
watch: Naturgy is a gas utility group; its Panama arm distributes electricity. Donor logos on the museum's site carry no names.
why_flagged: Private non-profit funded by companies and art lovers. Naturgy, a gas and electricity group, signed a sponsorship in April 2023 covering upkeep and operations.
records_note: Publishes annual reports for 2018 to 2025 and a named board; donor logos carry no names or date, and no financial statements are posted.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art and Design (MCAD)
funding: Run by De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde; Art Circle patrons and benefit auctions (2018, 15 Nov 2025) with Leon Gallery as auction partner.
watch: Donor list not published. Art Circle donors and 2025 benefit sponsors not listed; Funding the Future 2025 page returns 404. No controversy found.
records_note: Its Support, About and Downloads pages post no reports, accounts, named donors or board; it sits under De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde.

name: KALEKTAR research platform on Belarusian contemporary art
funding: German Federal Foreign Office (Civil Society Cooperation programme) and Rönne-Stiftung, per the platform's own about page
watch: Online archive, index and journal founded 2015; co-founder and editor-in-chief Sergey Shabohin lives and works in Białystok, which is used as the map point since the platform publishes no address.
records_note: Its About and Partners pages name funders, undated; the site posts no annual reports, accounts or board, only an editorial team and advisory council.

name: MOCAK
funding: Municipal museum of the City of Kraków, with a car-dealer partnership.
records_note: Partner logos are undated and the Museum Council is named, but no reports are posted; the city bulletin with accounts timed out.

name: Belarusian Council for Culture (Rada Kultury)
funding: European Union (ArtPower Belarus, €2M over 28 months, delivered with the Danish Cultural Institute); Danish Cultural Institute; listed partners ABBA, RESET!, Forum of National Platforms, NDF
watch: Founded 1 Oct 2020 as the Belarusian Culture Solidarity Fund, renamed Feb 2021; registered in Tallinn as MTÜ Valgevene Kultuuri Assotsiatsioon and represented in Warsaw and Vilnius; CEO Siarhiej Budkin. Reports 1,600+ cultural workers supported and 230+ projects by Oct 2025. Belarus's interior ministry designated it 'extremist' on 7 Jun 2022 and again on 24 Apr 2026.
records_note: It posts activity reports 2021 to 2025 and files accounts in Estonia; partners appear as undated logos, and the site names staff but no board.

name: Kupalaŭcy (Free Kupala Theatre in exile)
funding: Ticket sales; Polish Ministry of Culture (Culture Promotion Fund honorary award, 17 Mar 2025); EU ArtPower Belarus project grants; diaspora crowdfunding and guest co-productions with Polish theatres; funds for two projects via Pavel Latushka's foundation; Polish Theatre Institute residencies ended in 2024
watch: Troupe formed 6 Oct 2020 after the Janka Kupala National Theatre's company resigned en masse in Aug 2020; moved via Ukraine to Poland (Warsaw and Lublin). Actors earn about PLN 500 a show and the troupe describes its financing as near zero. Belarus declared its YouTube channel 'extremist material' in Feb 2024 and the troupe an 'extremist formation' on 13 Dec 2024; actors face warrants limiting travel.
records_note: The troupe has no website of its own, only social media and press coverage, so it publishes no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Museum of Free Belarus
funding: Project of the National Anti-Crisis Management (Pavel Latushka); 367 m2 premises at Foksal 11 provided by the City of Warsaw; Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage, Culture Support Fund (Digital Culture 2025 co-financing); individual donors via PayPal and crypto; Fundacja Białoruś Przyszłości
watch: Opened 17 Jul 2022 with Polish government backing; about 700 artefacts of the 2020 protest movement plus digital testimonies; cooperation agreements with Poland's National Institute of Museology, the Karta Foundation and the Hoover Institution; nominated for EMYA 2027 and longlisted for the Council of Europe Museum Prize; in July 2026 it says it is still seeking a permanent home.
records_note: A project of the National Anti-Crisis Management: no reports, accounts or funder list; the parent names its leadership and takes PayPal and crypto donations.

name: Ujazdowski Castle CCA
funding: State institution under the Ministry of Culture.
watch: 2020-24 directorship was politically contested, not a funding issue.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports or accounts that we found; the partners page shows logos with no dates and the board is not listed.
